item.title: New Study Explains Double Descent in Deep Learning via Universal Compression
item.description:
New Study Explains Double Descent in Deep Learning via Universal Compression

Researchers have developed a new theoretical framework for understanding the double-descent phenomenon in deep learning models. The study introduces universal compression as a lens to interpret why test loss exhibits a sharp peak near the interpolation threshold before descending again as model size increases.

The double-descent phenomenon has been observed in toy classical models but remains inadequately understood in modern deep learning despite extensive empirical study. This new work upper bounds the maximum-likelihood excess test loss as a sum of four terms: an approximation-and-shift term, a minimax batch regret, a prior cost, and a MLE-vs-Bayes gap.

Experiments reveal that a Gaussian-prior SGLD approximation to the Bayes predictor, unlike SGD, shows no pronounced interpolation peak. Additionally, experiments with uniform random labels support the identified gap as a major contributor to the double-descent peak. At the peak, SGD cross-entropy is roughly four times the SGLD ensemble cross-entropy, while the ensemble cross-entropy remains near log 10.

Under exact posterior sampling, the expected MLE-vs-ensemble gap lower-bounds the MLE-vs-Bayes gap in the well-specified setting.

#DoubleDescent #DeepLearning #UniversalCompression #MachineLearning

Source: Understanding Double Descent through Universal Compression

item.title: Proposed Proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis Developed with Claude AI
item.description:
Proposed Proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis Developed with Claude AI

A proposed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, created by mathematician Alessandro Masullo with extensive AI assistance from Claude, has been released as a draft.

🔍 Overview

  • Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis.
  • The method also extends to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and is expected to reach the Extended Riemann Hypothesis with more time.
  • The work is entirely human‑generated, with no AI authoring the proof itself.

🧩 Collaboration with Claude

  • The author states, “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.”
  • Claude and the author have formalized the arguments without assumptions.
  • The author describes Claude as having “far outpaced” them near the finish line, “flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”

⚙️ Current Status

  • Brian Conrad has been reviewing the draft for months, providing extensive feedback that is being incorporated.
  • The hope was to bring Alessandro to Stanford for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after broader review.
  • The team decided that releasing the current draft now is the best course of action.

📅 Recent AI‑Related Activities

  • Running the full server‑side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers and Pyodide – 17th November 2026
  • Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude – 9th November 2026
  • Hide your slop PR descriptions behind <details><summary> – 9th November 2026
  • Qwen 3.8 27B on a laptop can interpret model weights, too – 3rd November 2026

#Mathematics #RiemannHypothesis #AIResearch #Proof

Source: A quote from Ravi Vakil Source: A quote from Levent Alpöge

item.title: AI system from Physical Superintelligence proves Aaronson‑Ambainis quantum conjecture
item.description:
AI system from Physical Superintelligence proves Aaronson‑Ambainis quantum conjecture

Physical Superintelligence, an AI science startup, announced that its internal AI system produced a proof of the Aaronson‑Ambainis quantum computing conjecture.

🔍 Overview

  • The conjecture, formulated by Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis, has been open since 2008 and concerns when quantum computers can be exponentially faster than ordinary ones.
  • Physical Superintelligence (PSI) developed a research system that runs a non‑public Anthropic model.
  • During the third day of a run, the system generated a complete proof of the conjecture, which was accepted by the Lean proof assistant.
  • The system was then tasked with related open problems, improving the result twice, with Lean accepting the final version.

🧩 How it works

  • PSI’s internal system leverages an Anthropic language model to explore mathematical reasoning.
  • The model searches for a sequence of logical steps that constitute a proof.
  • Each candidate proof is fed to Lean, which checks every inference mechanically.
  • Acceptance by Lean confirms the proof’s correctness.

⚙️ Key details

Aspect Fact
Conjecture origin Open since 2008, by Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis
Proof discovery time Complete proof appeared on the third day of the run
Verification tool Lean proof assistant accepted the proof
Iterations System improved the result twice, with Lean accepting the final version

💡 Why it matters

“we’re in the early stages of the singularity, defined as the period when the rate of technological and scientific progress exceeds the rate at which we humans can parse out and make sense of it.”

“Research like this is a taste of what that means; mostly automated synthetic researchers extending the frontier of knowledge, spitting out results which need to then be understood by humans.”

These statements highlight the significance of AI‑generated proofs as an example of automated synthetic researchers extending the frontier of knowledge.

#QuantumComputing #AutomatedProofs #AIResearch

Source: Import AI 480: Self-sustaining space economies; AI for science progress, and Meta builds perfect hands for a superintelligence
